title: Paranormal Pizza celebrates rising from the ashes and getting a national nod
excerpt: Paranormal Pizza in South Bethlehem celebrates reopening after fire and earns third place in the 2026 VegNews best vegan pizzeria awards.
content:
There’s a lot to celebrate at Paranormal Pizza, a South Bethlehem vegan pizza shop with an X-Files theme. 

And co-owners Marc and Joey Kubushefski plan to celebrate their rise from the ashes and recent national recognition. 

However, it hasn’t been an easy road for the twin brothers’ business. 

The business sprung from the COVID-19 pandemic six years ago when the brothers, who are both vegan, were hungry for pizza but couldn’t find any vegan options during the shutdown. 

“It was very hard to get pizza as a vegan and the commercial vegan cheeses aren’t very good,” said Marc Kubushefski. “So, I taught myself how to make cashew cheese and pizza dough and started to make my own.” 

He liked the pizza he was making and told many of his vegan friends about his accomplishment. 

Friends tried it and liked it and soon he was getting calls from people looking to buy his pizza. 

He said they basically turned their kitchen into a pizza shop, but as demand grew, it was clear they would need a real commercial kitchen and a shop to sell their pizza out of. 

Their original location opened on the Northside of Bethlehem in 2022. Being X-Files fans, the brothers decided to create a paranormal theme naming pies after Mulder and Scully, the Lone Gunmen and even an Alien Bounty Hunter pizza. 

He said the theme was meant to make the pizza shop more of a destination. 

“There are only so many vegans in the Lehigh Valley,” Marc said. To succeed, the brothers knew they would have to draw vegan pizza fans from Philadelphia, New Jersey, New York and beyond specifically to experience the restaurant. 

The brothers offered a combination of a traditional version of vegan pizza that begins with naturally fermented sourdough and their homemade cashew mozzarella. 

They also have almond ricotta, sauces, seitan wings, pepperoni, sausage, chick’n and other toppings in-house. The entirely plant-based menu also includes Detroit-style pizzas alongside garlic knots, wings, cheesesteaks, sandwiches, loaded fries and rotating specials. 

The combination worked.  

“We were really busy. Business was growing steadily,” he said. 

They even grew a following among vegan musicians who were playing locally in the Lehigh Valley including Alkaline Trio, Dashboard Confessional, Gorilla Biscuits, JUDGE, Quicksand, Rise Against, Texas Is The Reason, and The Color Fred. 

But while they were enjoying their success – disaster struck. 

In February 2023, a devastating fire damaged the restaurant and forced it to close. 

A number of permitting and contractor issues prevented them from reopening as quickly as they wanted. 

So, the brothers took Paranormal Pizza on the road, serving vegan cheesesteaks and other vegan dishes they had become known for. They weren’t able to offer pizza because the size of the oven would be too big for a food truck. 

They also had pop-up restaurants, including one at Jay’s Local in Allentown. 

But as they struggled to get finances together to reopen a bricks and mortar restaurant of their own, their fans were getting impatient for their favorite pizza. 

When unexpected costs threatened to keep them from opening a new restaurant, the community rallied behind them. Supporters contributed $22,943 through crowdfunding, helping Paranormal Pizza complete its new home and reopen on Halloween 2025. 

Now, as the brothers are getting ready to celebrate one year in their new location, they’ve received another reason to celebrate. 

Paranormal Pizza was recently named one of America’s best vegan pizzerias, earning third Place and the Editors’ Vote for Best Vegan Pizzeria in the 2026 VegNews Restaurant Awards, which drew nearly 350,000 votes nationwide. 

As Halloween approaches, the brothers know their first anniversary in their new shop isn’t simply a celebration of one year in a new restaurant. It’s a celebration of the customers who followed them from one incarnation to the next, the community that helped them rebuild.
